questions.stem_markdown: A block of mass $12\,\text{kg}$ is being pulled by a rope up a rough plane. The plane is inclined at an angle of $20^\circ$ above the horizontal. The rope pulling the block is parallel to a line of greatest slope of the plane. The coefficient of friction between the block and the plane is $0.4$. The acceleration of the block is $2\,\text{m s}^{-2}$.\n\nFind the tension in the rope.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For use of N2L with 4 terms. Allow sign errors. Allow sin/cos mix. Allow $$g$$ missing. Allow with their Friction or just $$F$$.
Use of $$F = 0.4R$$ where $$R$$ is a component of weight, to get an equation in $$T$$ only.
AWRT 110 CWO.

questions.stem_markdown: Three coplanar forces of magnitudes $PN$, $5N$ and $10N$ act at a point $O$, as shown in the diagram. The resultant of the three forces has magnitude $QN$ and acts in a direction perpendicular to the force of magnitude $PN$.\n\nFind the value of $P$ and the value of $Q$.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For resolving in direction of $$P$$. 3 terms; allow sign errors and allow sin/cos mix.
Must be positive.
For resolving in direction of $$Q$$. 3 terms; allow sign errors and allow sin/cos mix.
Must be positive.

questions.stem_markdown: The diagram shows the velocity-time graph of the motion of a cyclist. The graph consists of three straight line segments. The cyclist passes a point $O$ with speed $3\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ and then accelerates for $10\,\text{s}$ with constant acceleration $0.5\,\text{m s}^{-2}$. He then travels at constant speed for $30\,\text{s}$ before decelerating, coming to rest at point $P$, covering a distance of $80\,\text{m}$ whilst decelerating.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Attempt to find time for deceleration. Using *their* 8.

parts.prompt_markdown: On a horizontal section of the road, the power of the lorry's engine is constant. There is a constant resistance to motion of $1600\,\text{N}$.
The steady speed which the lorry can maintain with the engine working at power $P\,\text{W}$ is $30\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.\n\nFind the value of $P$.
At an instant when the speed of the lorry is $16\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, its engine is working at a power of $40\,\text{kW}$.\n\nFind the acceleration of the lorry at this instant.

When the lorry has reached a speed of $20\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, it begins to ascend a section of road inclined at an angle $\alpha^\circ$ to the horizontal. The engine now works at a power of $120\,\text{kW}$. There is no change in the lorry's speed as it ascends the hill. The constant resistance to motion remains $1600\,\text{N}$.\n\nFind the value of $\alpha$.

skills: Use P=Fv with resistance to find the engine power at steady speed
Use power at an instant to find net force and acceleration
Apply energy/power balance on an incline with constant speed to find the angle
methods: Net force from power minus resistive work rate
Inclined-plane force component with constant speed
subtopics: Inclined plane with no speed change
Relating power to force and speed

Find the value of $v$ and the value of $w$.

questions.stem_markdown: When a particle $P$ of mass $m\,\text{kg}$ has speed $u\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, its momentum is $4\,\text{N s}$ and its kinetic energy is $16\,\text{J}$.\n\n$P$ is now projected on a smooth horizontal surface with speed $v\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ directly towards a particle $Q$ of mass $1.25\,\text{kg}$ which is stationary. After $P$ and $Q$ collide, the velocity of $P$ is $w\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ and the velocity of $Q$ is $2w\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. The loss of kinetic energy in the collision is $25\,\text{J}$.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Using *their* value of *m*. Correct number of terms, allow sign errors.
Using *their* value of *m*
For equation in *w* or *v* only. Dependent on the two previous **M** marks
For both. Use of *mg* in momentum **A0**

parts.prompt_markdown: It is given that the plane $BC$ is smooth.\n\nFind the tension in the string and the acceleration of $Q$.

It is given instead that the plane $BC$ is rough. The work done against the frictional force when $Q$ moves $2\,\text{m}$ down the plane is $1.8\,\text{J}$. You should assume that $P$ does not reach the pulley and that $Q$ does not reach $C$.\n\nUse an energy method to find the speed of $Q$ when it has moved $2\,\text{m}$ down the plane.

assets.description: A mechanics diagram showing a triangular setup with points A, B, and C. Point B is at the top of the triangle, with a mass of 0.3 kg at point P on the left side (AB) and a mass of 0.6 kg at point Q on the right side (BC). The angle at point A is labeled as θ°, and the angle at point C is labeled as 30°. The diagram includes a horizontal reference line from A to C.

equations: Sum of forces in the vertical direction at point B = 0
Sum of forces in the horizontal direction at point B = 0
Equilibrium condition for point P: Tension in AB = 0.3g * sin(θ°)
Equilibrium condition for point Q: Tension in BC = 0.6g * sin(30°)
relationships: Tension in AB and BC are related through the equilibrium at point B
The horizontal component of tension in AB and BC must balance
The vertical components of tension in AB and BC must balance the weights at P and Q

skills: For the smooth plane case, set up equations of motion for each mass to find tension and acceleration
For the rough plane case, use an energy method to find speed after a given displacement
methods: Newton’s second law with tension and component weights (smooth case)
Energy method with work done against friction (rough case)
subtopics: Tension in a light inextensible string
Dynamics of particles on smooth/rough inclines

questions.stem_markdown: Two particles, $P$ and $Q$, of masses $0.3\,\text{kg}$ and $0.6\,\text{kg}$ respectively, are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string. The string passes over a smooth pulley fixed at a point $B$ where the inclined planes $AB$ and $BC$ meet. $P$ lies on the smooth plane $AB$ which is inclined at an angle $\theta^\circ$ to the horizontal where $\sin \theta^\circ = 0.4$. $Q$ lies on the plane $BC$ which is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The string is taut and the particles can move on lines of greatest slope of the two planes (see diagram). The particles are released from rest.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Use of Newton’s second law for $P$ or $Q$ or system
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Allow $g$ missing. Correct number of terms. Allow $\sin/\cos$ mix. Allow sign errors. Allow using $\theta = 24^\circ$ or better.
A1 For any one correct equation. A2 For any two correct equations.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: For attempt to solve for $T$ or $a$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Must get to ‘$T$ = ‘ or ‘$a$ = ‘. From equations with the correct number of relevant terms.
Allow $\pm 2$.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: PE change for $P = \pm 0.3g \times 2 \times 0.4[= \pm 2.4]$ PE change for $Q = \pm 0.6g \times 2 \sin 30[= \pm 6]$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For either.
Attempt at work-energy equation. 4 terms; dimensionally correct. Allow sign errors. Do not allow missing $g$.

parts.prompt_markdown: Find the time at which $X$ is instantaneously at rest, and hence find the total distance travelled by $X$ between $t = 0$ and $t = 16$.
When the velocity of $Y$ is $-9.6\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, show that the displacement of $X$ from $O$ is equal to the displacement of $Y$ from $P$.

skills: Differentiate displacement to find velocity and solve for when velocity is zero
Compute distance travelled from t=0 to a specified time interval
Integrate acceleration to obtain velocity/displacement relationships or use given velocity to establish equality of displacements
methods: Use kinematic relations from a(t) to v(t) and displacement
Solve equations and substitute given velocity condition
subtopics: Displacement as a function of time
Acceleration and velocity for variable acceleration

questions.stem_markdown: A particle $X$ moves along a straight track, starting from a point $O$ at time $t = 0$. The displacement of $X$ from $O$ at time $t\,\text{s}$ is $s\,\text{m}$, where $s = 3t^{\frac{3}{2}} - 6t$.\n\nA second particle $Y$ moves along another straight track, starting from a point $P$ at time $t = 0$. The acceleration of $Y$ at time $t\,\text{s}$ is $a\,\text{m s}^{-2}$, where $a = 0.8 - 0.6t$. The velocity of $Y$ when it leaves $P$ is $7.5\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: The power of $t$ must decrease by 1 in at least 1 term with a change of coefficient in the same term.
Allow un-simplified.
For attempt to solve for $t$. Condone sign errors and transposing fractions. Correct squaring of $\sqrt{t}$.
Use of limits 0 and their $\frac{16}{9}$ or their $\frac{16}{9}$ and 16 correctly.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: For both i.e. $$F(16) - F\left(\text{their } \frac{16}{9}\right) - \left[ F\left(\text{their } \frac{16}{9}\right) - [F(0)] \right]$$ OR $$F(16) - F\left(\text{their } \frac{16}{9}\right) + \left[ F\left(\text{their } \frac{16}{9}\right) - [F(0)] \right]$$ OR $$F(16) - 2 \times F\left(\text{their } \frac{16}{9}\right)$$

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: AWRT 103 m
The power of $t$ must increase by 1 in at least 1 term with a change of coefficient in the same term.
